_readme: FILL THIS BY HAND. Only write what you can SEE in the video. Never guess.
You label the SOURCE CLIP ONLY -- the one ~8 second recording.
tt6.mp4 is that clip copied 4 times, so the scorer expands your labels x4
by itself. Do NOT write the same action four times.
Timing is relative to the START OF THE CLIP, so it runs 0.0 -> about 8.3.
Rough numbers are fine. 'timing_tolerance_sec' below is the slack the
scorer allows, so being half a second off costs nothing.
One entry in 'actions' per thing you do with your hands. If you do 2 things,
there are 2 entries. If 3, then 3. Delete the entries you do not need.
'i_see' is the most important field. Write it in your own plain words,
describing only what is visible. That is the record everything else is
checked against.
Allowed values for 'action' (pick exactly one, copy the spelling):
GRASP RELEASE PICK PLACE MOVE PUSH PULL OPEN CLOSE INSERT REMOVE
USE_TOOL TOUCH INSPECT UNKNOWN
-> If you are not sure, write UNKNOWN. That is a real answer, not a failure.
Allowed values for 'direction' (this is the field the pipeline keeps getting
backwards, so please be careful here):
INTO     = object ends up inside something
OUT_OF   = object ends up outside something it was inside
ONTO     = object ends up resting on top of a surface
OFF      = object is lifted off a surface
NONE     = no in/out or on/off meaning (e.g. just closing a lid)
Allowed values for 'hand': LEFT RIGHT BOTH CANNOT_TELL
JSON RULE that bites people: no comma after the LAST item in a list or
object. Everything else is just quotes and colons.
Delete the whole '_example_action' block before you send this back.

_example_action._note: THIS IS A FAKE EXAMPLE ABOUT A CUP, NOT YOUR VIDEO. Delete this block.
_example_action.i_see: my right hand lifts the white cup off the table and puts it on the shelf
